m29: 💡 Let the beef and cauliflower mix cool for 10 minutes before stirring in the Greek yogurt and ranch, otherwise the yogurt splits and turns watery in the container.
💡 Keeps 4 days in the fridge but does not freeze well once the yogurt is in; reheat at 70% microwave power, stirring halfway so the rice does not dry out.
m48: 💡 If you are prepping ahead, cook the tuna through rather than rare: rare tuna kept in a container for two days goes grey and mushy. Eat within 2 days, do not freeze.
💡 Eat this one cold or at room temperature; reheating seared tuna makes it dry and chalky. Salt the tomatoes and cucumber only on the day you eat, or the tabbouleh pools with liquid.
m32: 💡 Slice the steak thin across the grain and keep it medium at most; reheating well-done sirloin turns it leathery. Warm the steak and sweet potato for 60 seconds only and add the cucumber salad cold.
💡 Keeps 4 days refrigerated. Pack the lemon dressing in a small pot and toss with the cucumber and red onion just before eating, or the cucumber goes limp and waters everything down.
m50: 💡 Chicken breast in a slow cooker goes stringy past the point it shreds, so check from 5 hours on Low and pull it the moment the forks slide through. Reserve some cooking liquid to moisten the shredded meat.
💡 The pulled chicken freezes well for up to 3 months in its sauce; the sweet potato and brown rice are better made fresh each week. Fridge life is 4 days, reheat on full power with a spoon of broth.
hol2: 💡 Turkey breast dries out fast, so pull it as soon as a probe reads 72°C and let it sit in the broth while you portion; keep a little broth for the uncovered microwave reheat.

💡 Keep the blended cottage cheese gravy in a separate pot and spoon it over after reheating; microwaved cottage cheese splits and goes grainy. Turkey and squash freeze for 2 months, the green beans go soft after freezing.
hol5: 💡 Pack the Greek yogurt and the crispy onion topping in separate pots; yogurt left on the rice goes watery and the onions turn soggy. The lamb, lentil and rice base freezes well for 3 months.
💡 Spread the cooked brown rice on a tray to cool before folding it into the lamb, otherwise the steam turns it gluey. Keeps 4 days, reheat covered with a tablespoon of water at full power.
v2: 💡 Reheat the tofu and broccoli in an air fryer at 180°C for 5 minutes to bring the crust back; a microwave makes the tofu spongy. Keep the cottage cheese in its own pot and add it cold.
💡 Dry the pressed tofu cubes with kitchen paper and get the sesame oil properly hot before they go in, or they steam and stick instead of browning. Keeps 4 days, does not freeze once sauced.
v6: 💡 Reheat at 60% microwave power in 90-second bursts; full power turns the set eggs rubbery and squeaky. Keep the cottage cheese and feta in a separate pot and dollop on after heating.
💡 The sauce with chickpeas and spinach freezes well for 3 months, so freeze it in portions and poach fresh eggs into it when you reheat. With eggs included it keeps 3 days in the fridge, not longer.
v8: 💡 Pull the pasta 2 minutes before the packet time; it keeps softening in the sauce and again on reheating. Add the blended cottage cheese sauce off the heat, since simmering it makes it grainy.
💡 Keeps 4 days refrigerated but does not freeze, as the cottage cheese and milk sauce separates when thawed. Reheat at 70% power with a splash of milk and stir halfway to loosen it.
bf1: 💡 Cook the hashbrowns in a single layer and leave them alone until the underside browns before stirring, otherwise they steam into a grey mush. Do not crowd the pan with the peppers.
💡 Good for 4 days in the fridge. Reheat at 70% microwave power so the eggs stay tender, then crisp the bacon separately in a dry pan for a minute; pack the cherry tomatoes on top so they stay fresh.
bf2: 💡 If you are wrapping these ahead, leave the tomato and spinach out and add them cold after reheating; a wrapped tomato slice makes the bagel soggy by morning. Assembled sandwiches keep 3 days.
💡 Cook the egg through, not runny, if it is going in a wrap; a runny yolk leaks and goes rubbery on reheating. Reheat foil-wrapped in an air fryer at 160°C for 8 minutes rather than microwaving.
bf3: 💡 Protein powder batter browns fast and stays raw inside, so keep the pan on medium-low and make the pancakes no wider than 8 cm. Wring the grated carrot hard or the batter will not set.
💡 The pancakes keep 4 days refrigerated and freeze for a month with baking paper between them; reheat in a toaster or air fryer at 170°C for 3 minutes. Make the yogurt topping fresh.
bf5: 💡 Take the scrambled eggs off the heat while still glossy; they cook again in the microwave and dry out if fully set first. Reheat covered at 70% power with a tablespoon of water.
💡 The beef, egg and rice mix keeps 4 days and freezes for 2 months. Add the spinach and cherry tomatoes cold after reheating, since both collapse and weep if microwaved.
bf6: 💡 Let the beef and eggs cool completely before rolling; steam trapped in a warm burrito softens the tortilla and makes it split when toasted. Roll tight with the ends tucked in.
💡 Foil-wrapped burritos keep 4 days in the fridge or 2 months frozen. From frozen, remove the foil and microwave 2 minutes, then finish in an air fryer at 180°C for 5 minutes to crisp.
bf7: 💡 Whisk the whites and whole eggs together with a pinch of salt just before cooking and keep the pan on medium-low; the extra whites go rubbery fast on high heat. Stop while still slightly wet.

💡 This is a cook-fresh recipe: scrambled eggs made with this many whites turn watery after a night in the fridge. If you must prep, keep the eggs and toast in separate containers and reheat at 50% power.
bf9: 💡 Let the espresso cool for a minute and blend it with the cold milk before adding the whey; pouring whey straight into hot coffee makes it clump and curdle.
💡 Nothing here benefits from prepping ahead except halving the tomatoes and boiling the eggs; hard-boiled eggs keep 5 days unpeeled in the fridge. Store the cottage cheese in its own pot.
bf12: 💡 Turkey patties dry out quickly, so press a dimple into the centre of each and cook to 74°C rather than by colour. Cooked patties freeze for 2 months and are easy to reheat from frozen.
💡 Assembled bagels keep 3 days; for the 60-second microwave reheat, wrap in damp kitchen paper so the bagel does not go hard, and add the sliced tomato and spinach afterwards.
pw4: 💡 Cook the egg whites over medium-low with a mist of oil and fold gently rather than stirring constantly; high heat turns them squeaky and rubbery within seconds. Salt at the end.
💡 If prepping the whites ahead, portion them into pots for up to 3 days and reheat at 50% power for 45 seconds; toast and spread the jam fresh so the bread stays crisp.
sn2: 💡 Store the chicken filling and the bao buns separately for up to 3 days; filled buns go soggy overnight. Bao reheat best in a steamer for 4 minutes or a microwave with a damp cloth for 40 seconds.
💡 Reheat the chicken at 60% power and stir well; if the cottage cheese has separated in the fridge, a spoonful of freshly blended cottage cheese brings it back. Add the spring onion cold.
sn6: 💡 Minced chicken breast overcooks in seconds, so take it off the heat as soon as no pink remains and dress it while warm; the lime juice and soy soak in better and keep it moist.
💡 The dressed chicken keeps 4 days in the fridge and is meant to be eaten cold. Pack the lettuce cups, cucumber and herbs in a separate container, or they wilt in the lime dressing.
sn8: 💡 Put half the cheddar down first, then the chicken and pepper, then the rest on top; the cheese on both sides glues the tortilla shut so it does not fall apart when flipped.
💡 Cooked quesadillas keep 3 days; reheat in a dry pan over medium heat or an air fryer at 180°C for 4 minutes, never the microwave, which makes them chewy. Keep the yogurt and salsa in separate pots.
bf16: 💡 Use a banana that is still slightly firm and lay the slices in a hot pan without moving them for 2 minutes; a very ripe banana turns to mush before it caramelises.
💡 Whisk the whey into the yogurt slowly with a fork to avoid lumps, then chill it while you cook. This is a plate-and-eat breakfast; the banana and eggs do not hold up in the fridge.
bf20: 💡 Let the oats cool for a couple of minutes before stirring in the whey; adding it to boiling porridge makes it clump and can turn the texture chalky. Add a splash of milk to loosen it.
💡 Prepped porridge keeps 4 days refrigerated and thickens overnight, so reheat at 70% power with 50 ml of milk and stir halfway. The cinnamon apple compote freezes well in portions.
bf21: 💡 Stir the vanilla whey into the Greek yogurt with a few drops of water until smooth, and spread the almond butter to the edges of the toast as a barrier so the yogurt does not soak in.
💡 The protein yogurt and chopped dates can be prepped and kept 4 days in a pot; toast the bread and brown the banana fresh, as fried banana goes slimy after a night in the fridge.
bf23: 💡 Stop whisking as soon as the lumps are gone and leave the batter to rest; overmixing a protein pancake mix knocks the air out and gives flat, chewy pancakes. Flip only once bubbles reach the centre.
💡 Cooked pancakes keep 3 days refrigerated or a month frozen with baking paper between them; a toaster on a medium setting warms them from frozen in one go. Add the strawberries and syrup cold.
bf25: 💡 Dice the sweet potato no bigger than 1.5 cm and leave the pieces alone for the first 5 minutes so they crisp before you smash them; constant stirring gives you soft, pale cubes.
💡 Rest the tenderloin for 3 minutes before slicing so the juices stay in the meat. If prepping ahead, keep the steak medium-rare and reheat only 45 seconds at 50% power; fry the eggs fresh.
bf26: 💡 Pull the eggs off the heat while they still look slightly wet; the egg whites carry on setting in the residual heat and dry out if you wait for them to look done in the pan.

💡 Assemble this fresh: smoked salmon should never be reheated, and mashed avocado browns within hours even with lemon. If prepping, keep salmon, cottage cheese and tomatoes in separate pots for up to 2 days.
bf27: 💡 Squeeze the shredded sweet potato in a clean tea towel until no more liquid comes out, then press it into a thin layer in the pan; wet shreds steam rather than crisp.

💡 Cook the mushrooms in a single layer on high heat without salt until golden, then season; salting early draws out water and they boil. Hash and mushrooms keep 3 days and reheat in an air fryer at 180°C.
bf28: 💡 Cottage cheese down the centre acts as a moisture barrier, so keep it there and put the tomatoes on top of the eggs, not against the wrap, or the tortilla goes soggy within an hour.
💡 If you want this ready for the week, scramble the eggs slightly underdone and store them for 3 days; assemble the wrap on the day, as sliced avocado browns and spinach wilts once rolled.
bf29: 💡 Poached eggs can be made ahead: drop them into iced water once done, keep in the fridge up to 3 days, and reheat in barely simmering water for 60 seconds. The egg whites are best scrambled fresh.
💡 Use eggs as fresh as possible and strain off the loose white in a sieve before poaching; old eggs spread into ragged wisps regardless of how much vinegar you add.
bf30: 💡 Squeeze the wilted spinach dry before it goes into the omelette; the water it releases stops the eggs setting and gives you a wet, torn fold. Add the feta last so it stays in pockets.
💡 Cook the omelette on medium-low and pull the set edges toward the middle, tilting the pan so raw egg runs underneath; high heat browns and toughens the whites before the centre is cooked.
bf31: 💡 Egg whites without yolks stick and tear easily, so use a well-seasoned non-stick pan on medium-low and do not touch them until the edges lift. A lid for the last minute sets the top gently.
💡 Roast the pumpkin and sauté the mushrooms in a batch; they keep 4 days in the fridge, so each morning is just the whites. Reheat the veg for 30 seconds before adding to the omelette.
m63: 💡 Brown the mince in two batches so it sears rather than boils in its own liquid; grey, steamed mince gives a flat ragu. The sauce freezes for 3 months in portions.
💡 Cook the pasta 2 minutes short and toss with a spoon of reserved pasta water before portioning; it finishes cooking on reheating. Keeps 4 days, reheat covered at 70% power, parmesan added after.
m64: 💡 Toss the pesto through the pasta off the heat and reheat later at 60% power only; bringing a cottage cheese sauce to a boil splits it into grainy curds. Do not freeze.
💡 The blanched kale keeps the pesto green, but it still dulls after 3 days, so this is a short-week recipe. Storing the pesto in a pot with a film of lemon juice on top helps it stay bright.
m65: 💡 Whisk the miso into warm, not boiling, pasta water and add it with the pan off the heat; boiling miso makes it bitter and, with the cottage cheese, grainy. Keeps 4 days.
💡 Pack the crispy leeks and sesame seeds in a separate pot and add after reheating, otherwise they go soft in the container. Reheat at 60% power with a splash of water.
